title: Photonz only offers an update once that version can actually be downloaded
goal: Photonz decided 0.19.0 was out because the website's version file said so, before the download existed, and updating failed with a server error. The update check should only offer a version once its download is really there, and a failed download should say plainly that the update is not ready yet.
notes: User, 2026-10-25: 'i just tried to update photonz and it said server error' and 'why is photonz detecting 0.19 if we haven't published it yet'. Cause, verified in the intake window: Sources/Photonz/UpdateChecker.swift reads https://dzearing.github.io/photonz/version.json and trusts it; the release skill committed site/version.json with the tag, so the site deployed 0.19.0 in 2.5 minutes while the Release workflow needed about 20 to publish the DMG; Sources/Photonz/SelfUpdater.swift then got a 404 from releases/download/v0.19.0/Photonz.dmg and threw downloadFailed('the server returned an unexpected response'). The skill is fixed (e493d70c: the site is announced only after the DMG answers); this task makes the app safe on its own too.
acceptance: The update check offers version N only when the download for N answers (a HEAD request on releases/download/vN/Photonz.dmg returns 200 after redirects); otherwise it reports the app is up to date. The decision logic is in PhotonzCore with tests first (version file says newer + download answers = offer; version file says newer + download 404 = up to date; network error = the existing failure message).

If a download still fails part way, the message is plain and human, for example 'This update isn't ready to download yet. Try again in a few minutes.', never 'the server returned an unexpected response'.

MEASURED against the real servers: with the current release published, the check offers nothing on a build of that version and offers it on a build stamped one version lower; with a version number that has no release (a test stub of version.json), it offers nothing.
Try path: an installed older Photonz, Check for Updates while a release is half out: it says up to date, then offers the update once the download is published.

log.note: Reproduced on the real servers: version.json says 0.21.0 and its DMG answers 200; v0.99.0 (a version with no release) answers 404, which the old check never asked about (it compared version numbers only).

Built: PhotonzCore UpdateOffer.decide (HEAD on the DMG only when newer; answers=offer, missing=up to date, unreachable=failure message) and UpdateDownloadFailure.message, tests first (Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/UpdateOfferTests.swift). UpdateChecker.probeDownload does the HEAD; SelfUpdater.download throws downloadRefused(httpStatus:) with the plain sentence. Probe-only --update-check-diag (Sources/Photonz/Playtest/UpdateCheckerDiag.swift) measures the real servers.

Measured with the probe against dzearing.github.io + GitHub releases: as 0.21.0 -> up to date; as 0.20.0 -> offers 0.21.0; stub version.json naming 0.99.0 -> up to date (as 0.21.0 and as 0.20.0); stub naming 0.21.0 as 0.20.0 -> offers 0.21.0; download of v0.99.0 -> "This update isn't ready to download yet. Try again in a few minutes." Scripts/test.sh exit 0.

Chose "up to date" over a separate "update coming" state while a release is half out because the checklist asks for it and a person can do nothing with the in-between state; left rough in the audit, not filed.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples
